blocks.text: A comprehensive collection of finished case studies spanning 3D design, real-time audio-reactive systems, generative design pipelines and adaptive typographic campaigns.

caseStudies.title: Amplified Spaces
caseStudies.descShort: Amplified Spaces explores the transformation of music into immersive visual environments.
caseStudies.descLong: Using TouchDesigner to create real-time, audio-reactive visuals and Blender to construct architectural installations, the project visualizes tracks by artist Tom Vernon as large-scale experiential spaces.

process.title: TouchDesigner Engine
process.text: TouchDesigner was used to create all the visuals for this project. By building different node structures, I was able to handle everything from audio processing and beat recognition to real-time visual adjustments and post-processing effects.

process.title: B17
process.text: For B17, I wanted to create a retro CRT television effect to perfectly reflect the dusty, low-fidelity aesthetic of the track.

process.title: Fading Away
process.text: Fading Away displays a live visual spectrum that responds dynamically to different frequency bands, turning the song's audio waves into flowing, organic movements.

process.title: Onjuku
process.text: For Onjuku, the visuals translate into a slow-rotating ambient world, featuring fluid color distortions that are procedurally tied to the warm color palette of the album artwork.

process.title: Exhibition Gallery
process.text: After generating the visuals, I integrated them into 3D spaces designed to resemble modern, concrete-built exhibition rooms — adding lighting, ambient figures, and environmental storytelling elements. Each scene creates a simulated gallery experience where sound, light, and movement converge into unified, immersive encounters.

caseStudies.title: Handheld Stories
caseStudies.descShort: An interactive digital exhibition for the British Museum's Netsuke collection, reimagining traditional museum displays into tactile storytelling walkthroughs.
caseStudies.descLong: This project reimagines the traditional museum experience for the British Museum's Edo-period Netsuke carvings. By gathering 3D Sketchfab models and rotoscoping assets, I designed a fluid digital catalog concept. To represent the user's journey, I directed and sequenced a high-fidelity motion simulation showing interactive tactile transitions.

process.title: The Brief
process.text: For this project, the brief was to design a branding system for an exhibition on the British Museum's collection of Netsuke. Netsuke are small, intricately carved wooden and ivory sculptures from Edo-period Japan. I wanted to design an experience that felt highly tactile, celebrating the scale and craftsmanship of these small artifacts.

process.title: Preparing Assets
process.text: To construct the interface layouts, I gathered high-fidelity 3D scans of the Netsuke carvings from Sketchfab, using them to create detailed rotoscoped outlines and isolated 3D wireframe visuals. Shifting these detailed textures into digital silhouettes allowed me to build structural assets for the digital catalog pages.

process.title: Website Concept Outcome
process.text: Since I didn't know how to write code or build interactive websites at the time of this project, I instead animated and composited a short walkthrough video inside Premiere Pro and After Effects. This simulation shows what a user's tactile journey would look like, guiding viewers through interactive orbits, descriptions, and catalog sweeps.

caseStudies.title: Remnants
caseStudies.descShort: Inventing an ancient civilization through visual systems. Translating tactile museum traces and digital glyphs into towering, surreal landscapes.
caseStudies.descLong: What if writing did not exist in our culture, and we had to invent it from scratch? This project chronicles the creation of Haa'sk and Cra'sk—two fictional written scripts born from tactile markings and environmental textures found in our surroundings. Tracing these natural lines and geometric forms in Photoshop, I isolated and built a complete typographic catalog of nine vector glyphs. Seeking to manifest these symbols physically, I utilized Stable Diffusion to translate the glyphs into towering, surreal stone ruins set within desolate landscapes. These monolithic frames were then sequenced in After Effects to the atmospheric waves of Bliss Signal's 'Ambi Drift'—slowing the velocity to 60% to convey immense weight and historical scale.

process.title: Artifact Study & Found Forms
process.text: The journey began with a research visit to the Pitt Rivers Museum to select and study historical artifacts. I carefully analyzed their physical details, finding unique, raw forms hidden within the contours of ancient masks, decorated shields, and iron weights. Tracing these museum artifacts formed the organic foundation of my invented written scripts.

process.title: Stable Diffusion & ControlNet
process.text: To translate my 2D vector glyphs into towering neolithic ruins, I utilized ControlNet inside Stable Diffusion. By feeding the vector outlines directly into the model as hard structural guides, I was able to actively influence and command the architectural forms that the AI generated, ensuring they followed the precise contours of my script.

process.title: Fictional Alphabets in Glyphs
process.text: These are the final refined glyphs, compiled into a fully typeable digital typeface within the Glyphs App. By carefully perfecting their bounding boxes, line weight consistencies, and mathematical alignments, I successfully created a functional font where each symbol represents the finalized ancient characters.

process.title: Photoshop Asset Preparation
process.text: To prepare the stone structures for three-dimensional movement, I separated the glyphs from their environments in Photoshop. Using precise lasso masks, I cut the symbols into individual floating segments, then utilized Content-Aware Fill to recreate the sky and desert plates behind them, ensuring no blank space would show during animation.

caseStudies.title: Powersurge
caseStudies.descShort: A collaborative visual journey exploring the exponential growth of computing power, translating Moore's Law and historical FLOPS data into a dynamic, data-driven simulation.
caseStudies.descLong: Created in collaboration with Suyash Sunar, this project functions as a 'Data Portrait' mapping rapid computing advances. Sourcing historical supercomputer FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second) datasets spanning 30 years, we explored Moore's Law—the observation that technological capacity doubles exponentially. We integrated this raw curve directly into a TouchDesigner particle system to drive parameters like size, speed, and feedback chaotic transformations. The resulting real-time generative artwork represents the rapid digitization of the human race.

process.title: Concept & The Exponential Curve
process.text: Drawing inspiration from Mike Luan's 'Data Portraits', we wanted to explore using raw digital metrics to directly influence generative art, giving the artwork a hidden organic meaning. We mapped out 30 years of global supercomputer FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second) datasets from Our World in Data, reflecting the rapid growth predicted by Moore's Law. This timeline spreadsheet mapped every 10 seconds of video to a year of real-world computing history.

process.title: TouchDesigner Generative Engine
process.text: We built a generative network in TouchDesigner using a cylinder as the base emitter, and normalized the coordinates to constrict the particles into a sphere. An Animation CHOP locked the data curve to the master timeline, feeding the FLOPS values into multiple parameters. As computing capability scales, the data progressively drives particle size, speed, and green/red color values, leading to a chaotic bloom effect driven entirely by the feedback loops.

process.title: Visual Feedback Experiments
process.text: We ran multiple visual experiments to balance particle lifetime, speed, and feedback limits. The exponential nature of the curve meant that for over 75% of the timeline, the sphere remains quiet and highly structured, changing very slightly. It is only in the final seconds that the transition spikes dramatically, erupting into a beautifully chaotic firestorm of glowing, blooming particles.

process.title: Final Audio-Visual Assembly
process.text: The final data portrait was assembled in Premiere Pro. We overlayed the After Effects FLOPS timeline along the bottom, visualizing the curve as a white indicator circle keyframed along the X-axis. A digital year countdown created by Suyash was nested in the top-left corner, anchoring each visual state to its corresponding historical year, all paired with a brooding ambient soundscape.

caseStudies.title: Marimekko Exhibition
caseStudies.descShort: Comprehensive exhibition identity system for a theoretical Marimekko retrospective at the Saatchi Gallery, translating bold 2D prints into a cohesive spatial branding experience.
caseStudies.descLong: This comprehensive project establishes a bold, institutional exhibition identity system for a theoretical retrospective of the iconic Finnish design company, Marimekko, at the Saatchi Gallery. Drawing inspiration from Armi Ratia’s founding philosophy of self-expression and anti-elitist design, the system celebrates pattern diversity and structured wayfinding. I curated four legendary Marimekko designers—Maija Isola, Annika Rimala, Antti Kekki, and Fujiwo Ishimoto—incorporating their distinct styles into a cohesive color-coded journey. The visual system scales dynamically across typography permutations, promotional poster series, printed tickets, architectural maps, and motion advertisements.

process.title: The Brand: Anti-Elitist Design
process.text: Founded in 1951 by Armi Ratia, Marimekko is a pioneering Finnish design company renowned for its bold patterns, vibrant colors, and timeless aesthetics. From the beginning, the brand's core philosophy has focused on self-expression and positive empowerment. By celebrating equality, inclusivity, and anti-elitist design, Marimekko's architectural shapes and colorful fabrics became a liberating visual language for free-spirited women of all ages, sizes, and backgrounds.

process.title: The Creators: Four Artists
process.text: To capture the diverse spirit of the brand, I curated a retrospective focusing on four legendary Marimekko artists chosen for their popularity and distinct graphic styling. I analyzed and redrew their core repeating motifs: Antti Kekki's sharp geometric cutouts (Rappu, Patikka, Lauha, Heinikko); Maija Isola's organic, bold natural forms (Kalasääski, Leylah, Koppelo, Staccato); Annika Rimala's striking, structural graphic repeats (Aitu, Laine, Petrooli, Pikkusuomo); and Fujiwo Ishimoto's delicate, nature-inspired minimalism (KevatTalkoot, Kuiskaus, Taivas, Vihma).

caseStudies.title: Smuggler's Outpost
caseStudies.descShort: Set in a Dune-inspired universe, this project explores AI as an ideation partner in environment design, shifting from algorithmic generation to manual 3D modelling.
caseStudies.descLong: Exploring the workflow synergy of machine learning ideation and high-fidelity CGI. Sourcing visual elements from brutalist concrete forms and Sandworm-populated desert terrains, this project explores AI as a creative collaborator in environment design. By using Stable Diffusion prompt engineering and local inpainting to conceptualize a hidden Fremen spice-smuggling outpost carved into canyon walls, the design was successfully migrated into Blender for high-fidelity terrain sculpting, modular container modeling, realistic sand material mapping, and volumetric light path execution.

process.title: Project Concept & Dune Influence
process.text: This project explores AI as a creative collaborator in environment design, focusing on the early stages of concept development where ideas are most fluid. The goal was to design a hidden spice-smuggling outpost embedded within a narrow desert canyon, blending Fremen ingenuity with subtle off-world industrial elements. The project is set directly in the brutalist, sandworn cinematic universe of Frank Herbert’s Dune, emphasizing monolithic concrete structures, rusted landing pads, concealed tunnels, and half-buried cargo containers carved into sheer canyon walls. Below, you can explore the reference screenshots from the Dune films that established the core lighting direction, atmospheric tone, and architectural style of the scene.

process.title: Concept Prompt Engineering & AI Generation
process.text: To translate the initial concept into a high-fidelity visual blueprint, I utilized Stable Diffusion (SDXL) and custom LoRA models. The process focused heavily on meticulous prompt iteration—refining basic environmental descriptions into complete cinematic frames. I utilized local inpainting grids to isolate and refine complex structures like landing pads and hidden tunnels. Rather than treating AI as a simple automatic generator, it functioned as an active creative partner to explore lighting, scale, and visual serendipity. Below, you can view the six initial Stable Diffusion generated concept drafts that explored various sand textures, monolithic placements, and rocky architectures.

process.title: Final AI Concept Image
process.text: The final visual concept generated through prompt engineering and SDXL inpainting. This flat 2D render serves as the primary blueprint for the 3D blockout stage, establishing the core lighting direction, brutalist canyon structure, warm atmospheric color scheme, and modular building scales.

process.title: 3D Viewport Realization
process.text: With the concept locked, I migrated the environment design into Blender to construct the full 3D viewport. Having learned Blender from scratch for this project, I sculpted the high-walled canyon rocks, modeled custom structural cargo buildings, aligned realistic brutalist geometry, and mapped detailed materials. I configured realistic desert lighting paths matching the warm tones of the original concept. Key beginner hurdles including UV texture stretching, camera scale, and slow rendering times were solved through rigorous trial-and-error.

process.text: The final output features multiple high-fidelity camera renders and a fully realized cinematic video loop. caseStudies.title: The World Plays Here
caseStudies.descShort: A copy-led campaign for Xbox celebrating the borderless nature of modern gaming. Shifts focus onto the human experience with an inclusive aesthetic and 3D motion design.
caseStudies.descLong: Designing for a massive global community required an adaptable, culturally agnostic visual approach. Grounded in research of copywriting-driven brands, this campaign relies on powerful copy-led storytelling designed to unite players under a shared manifesto: 'The World Plays Here.' Kinetic typographic systems were paired with bold 3D motion design rotating around a simulated Earth globe in Blender, composited cleanly across digital and physical mockups in After Effects.

process.title: About the D&AD Brief
process.text: The D&AD brief challenged creatives to design a copy-led campaign celebrating gamers wherever and however they play ('Play Anywhere'). Xbox believes that games are about people and human experiences, not hardware, software, or static boxes. The goal was to reach diverse gaming niches around the globe (RPG, cosy-core, shooters) and build an emotional connection of shared belonging. Slogan development led to 'The World Plays Here', reframing the campaign around community and global inclusion.

process.title: Blender 3D Modeling & Setup
process.text: Translating the copy-first concept into 3D motion involved importing an Earth model and enveloping it in a spherical representation of the Xbox logo. To animate this concept, I separate the single-mesh logo into four distinct quadrants. I manually reset origin points to the Earth's geometric center for clean curves, worked in orthographic view for precise Y-axis pivot alignment, added cloud rotations, and fine-tuned spatial lighting. Below you can explore the complete matrix of 12 high-resolution workspace progress captures in our interactive grid gallery.

process.title: AE Compositing & Outcomes
process.text: Post-production was completed inside After Effects and Premiere Pro. I exported Blender renders as PNG transparent sequences to preserve alpha, designed a gradient-mapped space starfield aligning with Xbox brand guidelines, and resolved grey viewport shadows via opacity-masked brightness corrections. Sound design manually mixes the classic Xbox startup sound with AI-generated voiceover, synced to dynamic rising typography keys. process.title: Responsive Multi-Device Adaptations
process.text: Digital extensions showcase how the campaign is adapted for social and online feeds. The YouTube mockup simulates a sidebar video ad, built by keying out active video blocks on genuine desktop screenshots to retain native browser player controls and surrounding page elements. Mobile Instagram designs integrate portrait posters into phone mockups, removing black borders via color keying and layering official Xbox profile branding for ultimate credibility. In this section, you can toggle between 7 high-resolution device mockups.
